title: Microsoft Teams: allowed list of external meeting notetaker bots
summary: The roadmap facts and existing administrative controls are supported. The briefing should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft documentation about bot blocking and who can admit bots, and narrow its unverified statement about transcript storage. General Teams licensing and the missing lobby-admission checklist row also need minor corrections.

claims.claim: Teams plans an administrator-configured list of external meeting bots allowed to join meetings.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to configure a list of external meeting bots which are allowed to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.claim: Administrators will be able to block all other bots.
claims.quote: Admins can also opt to block all other bots

claims.claim: Administrators can instead send other bots through the currently available high friction lobby experience.
claims.quote: or let them be enforced into the currently available high friction lobby experience.

claims.claim: Meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate for allowed bots.
claims.quote: and meeting policies will be enforced as appropriate.

claims.claim: The planned organizational control concerns meetings hosted in the administrator's organization, not meetings hosted elsewhere.
claims.quote: controls for managing external bots and their access to meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn admin setting, PowerShell operation or API for the planned named allowed-bots list was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "allowed" "bots" "list" "PowerShell". Read manage-external-bots, teams-bot-identification and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; none documents an admin setting or API for a named allowed-bots list.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The briefing records licensing as unknown because no feature-specific licensing requirement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the schema's product-level licensing rule. Use: 'Teams requires a Teams license for each organizational user except anonymous meeting join. No licensing requirement specific to the planned allowed-bots list is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence requirement or meter specific to the planned allowed-bots list is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed list external meeting notetaker bots 580451 allowlist default licensing PowerShell; "Teams" "notetaker" "bots" "license". Read roadmap, manage-external-bots and user-access; no feature-specific licence or meter found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The existing external-bots Learn page lists no licence requirement or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policies external bots allowed list licensing meter; "Teams" "notetaker" "bots" "license". Read manage-external-bots in full; it states no licence requirement or meter.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn do not explain how entries on the planned list identify or match a bot.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting bots list bot identity matching Bot Identification Program storage transcripts blocked participant override admin role. Read roadmap, manage-external-bots and teams-bot-identification; no planned-list matching rules found.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not explain which existing behaviour it calls the high friction lobby experience.
claims.quote: or let them be enforced into the currently available high friction lobby experience.

claims.claim: Existing Teams bot detection uses signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: With detection enabled, detected bots wait in the lobby irrespective of the meeting's lobby configuration.
claims.quote: The participants detected as bots are placed in the meeting lobby irrespective of the lobby configuration for the meeting.

claims.claim: Detected bots require an organizer to admit them.
claims.quote: Even when a meeting allows participants to bypass the lobby, detected bots still require organizer approval before joining.
claims.fix: Acknowledge the qualification on the other cited page. Replace the admission wording in What's changing and the risk rationale with: 'Detected bots require explicit admission; the external-bots guidance says presenters can also admit them depending on the meeting setting.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots.

claims.claim: The existing policy defaults to When detected, require approval before joining, represented by RequireApprovalWhenDetected.
claims.quote: | When detected, require approval before joining | *RequireApprovalWhenDetected* | (**default**) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting. |

claims.claim: The documented existing choices are detect and require approval, or do not detect bots.
claims.quote: | Do not detect bots | *AllowBots* | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings. |
claims.fix: Replace the two-options wording in controls[1].note, its rendered table note and Why it matters with: 'The external-bots guide lists detection with approval and no detection. The cited Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference additionally documents BlockDetectedBots to block detected external bots.' Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps.

claims.claim: The setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: This setting is present in the Meeting Join and Lobby section of Meeting policies. Look for **"Manage external bots and their access to meetings"** and select the appropriate option.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected configures approval for detected bots.
claims.quote: **RequireApprovalWhenDetected**: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: The existing external-bots setting is scoped through meeting policies at user or group level.
claims.quote: **Scope**: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: The existing setting can be configured through the default org-wide policy or targeted policies for users or groups.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: The existing external-bots guidance marks itself as applicable to meetings, not events.
claims.quote: **APPLIES TO:**![Image of a checkmark for yes](/en-us/office/media/icons/success-teams.png) Meetings ![Image of a x for no](/en-us/office/media/icons/cancel-teams.png) Events

claims.claim: External meeting bots may record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.
claims.quote: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.claim: External meeting bots may store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organization's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: The planned list does not itself limit where an allowed bot stores transcripts.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams allowed external meeting bots list bot identity matching Bot Identification Program storage transcripts blocked participant override admin role. Read roadmap, manage-external-bots and teams-bot-identification; none states the planned list's transcript-storage behaviour.
claims.fix: Replace 'The list approves a bot; it does not by itself limit where that bot stores transcripts.' with 'The roadmap does not describe transcript-storage restrictions for allowed bots.'

claims.claim: Some external bots may not be detected.
claims.quote: Some external bots may not be detected.

claims.claim: Existing bot detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.
claims.quote: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.

claims.claim: A misclassified participant can be admitted from the lobby and marked This is not a bot.
claims.quote: When you observe this misclassification in the meetings, you can rectify the situation by admitting the participants from the lobby and marking them with "This is not a bot" option.

claims.claim: The Teams Bot Identification Program is described as a public preview for software vendors.
claims.quote:
## Microsoft Teams Bot Identification Program (Public Preview)

Microsoft is also introducing the Teams Bot Identification Program to support independent software vendors (ISVs) that build meeting bot experiences for Teams.

claims.claim: Eligible bot providers can register and include a self-identification marker in meeting join requests.
claims.quote: Through this program, eligible bot providers can register with Microsoft and include a self-identification marker in their meeting join requests.
